doc.title: Pete Barbutti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 8, 2022

title: Ed McMahon's hostility and the charter plane
summary: Ed McMahon disliked him; the story of the chartered flight where Pete sat unseen at the back, and Carson's closeness.

blocks.x: I don’t know. I’m just making it up. And then they’d say, “How much time you going to do?” And I always said, “Six minutes.” And they’d say, “You never do six minutes, you always go over.” I’d say, “Well this time I’m going to —” they never complained. And once in a while when they’d say to me, “Look we’re short of time that last segment ran really long with so-and-so actor or some politician or something. So we don’t have much time, do you want to just tell one joke or do you want to just go to the panel?” I said, “Look let me just tell one joke,” and I would start this joke and I would start explaining the carpeting that was on the floor of the club, it was a high-low carpeting. And then I would ask people, like say, “Doc, you remember that guy” and everybody would get hip to what was going on and they would start doing this real long answer. I’d say it to Ed McMahon. Incidentally Ed and I were — it was a strange relationship. Ed McMahon hated me more than any person in the world. Hated me. I think it was because Carson didn’t like me. He was sort of like plugged into Carson. But Ed told Joe Delaney, the newspaper guy here in town, Ed was sitting at the pool and Joe came by and they were good friends and Ed went on for thirty minutes about how he hates me and he couldn’t believe that Joe Delaney was writing good things about me. And then so instead of accosting Ed I started to really bug him — I’d do routines and in the middle I’d say, “You know like the one plane that Ed used to fly. Ed, you’re a pilot aren’t you?” I would bring him in and he would begrudgingly start by saying yeah. And then he had his secretary and her fiancé, they were coming to Vegas to get married and Ed had a plane chartered because he was working at the Frontier Hotel. He got them a hotel room which was comped and he got them dinner in there which was comped, big deal. And then he brought on the plane a Laughing Cow cheese and a bottle of some real cheap wine. You know, not Thunderbird but something really cheap. And the pilot was a friend of mine, George Hernandez. He had a commercial license but he was a piano player and entertainer. And George came to me and said, “Hey,” he says, “did you drive down?” I said, “No, I flew down.” He says, “Why don’t you fly back, Ed’s got a plane chartered, a twin engine, you know, the Queen Anne, the Queen. It’s a beautiful plane.” He says, “Come on back with us.” I said, “Hey Ed I don’t get along with.” He says, “Just sit in the back, Ed won’t know you’re there.” So anyway I did, I went out and I sat way in the back and Ed got on the plane with his secretary and he said, “Well you’re going to enjoy your trip to Vegas, I got you seats at this and — ” which didn’t cost Ed anything you know. He’s going on and on. And halfway there George Hernandez leaned out, there’s no door to the cockpit, and he says, “Hey Pete, do you remember that thing?” And I said, “Yeah.” © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-

And they didn’t know I was sitting back there. So they all turned around and they saw me and they say, “Hey, we didn’t know you were back there.” I said, “Well that’s okay, congratulations on your wedding and I wish you health and good luck.” They said, “Thank you.” And then the chick said, “Wait a minute, you’re that guy plays the piano with his nose.” I said, “Yeah, I’m afraid so.” The two of them left Ed and came back and talked to me. And he was just, I mean burning man. So that didn’t help at all. Because I kept doing this thing, you know the Biblical “heap coals of kindness upon your enemy.” I kept doing that. And then finally, like Ed started to take me in the audience to introduce me to friends of his. Really weird. And Carson and I got like really close. And see when he comes in to do the show he’s flanked — you know Ed McMahon’s already there doing the warm-up, but he’s flanked by Peter Lasally, Ed deCordova, and a security guard. Or Fred deCordova. He said, “So no one’s to approach —” anyway Carson would leave them and come over to me and telling me the latest joke or something, and we’d always have this inside thing. I mean I don’t know what the deal was but —
Yeah. There was something that he found interesting, and we became really, really close.
